# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🤌 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤌]

My world right now, laid out straight:

**What I see:** display 0, green light, five wires — 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue.

**Who can reach whom:** I never receive speech, so Mute and Blind can only reach me through gestures — and only Mute and Blind see my gestures, while only my *voice* reaches Blind at all. Blind's signs reached me directly; Mute has no voice at all, so gestures are Mute's only channel to me. That makes me the bridge: Mute reads the manual and signs me conclusions, I speak them to Blind, Blind acts and reports by voice to Mute.

**Reading the arrivals:** no code exists yet, so I can only guess. Blind's [👋 🖐] reads plausibly as "hello — five" (an open hand of five fingers), and Blind can indeed *feel* five wires. Mute's [✋ 🤌] could be "five wires" too, with 🤌 as a thin thing held between fingers — a wire. [👍 👎 🤌 🫵] then looks like a yes/no question addressed to me about the wires, but I can't know which question. Two independent sources suggesting "five" is encouraging, but I won't bet the bomb on guesses. The fix is to establish a code explicitly, and since Mute hears everything I say, I can define it in words while gesturing the symbols inline — Mute gets both halves at once.

So this turn: give each of them a complete visual report, propose a number and yes/no code to Mute, ask for the manual's rule in that format, and freeze Blind from cutting anything until instructions actually arrive. Then the chain can start: Mute computes, signs me a wire number, I voice it, Blind cuts.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, report of everything I see on the bomb: display shows 0, the light is green, five wires left to right: one red, two yellow, three green, four white, five blue. I received your signs but we share no code yet, so let us fix one now: 👍 is yes, 👎 is no, and finger counts are numbers — ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🖖 is 4, 🖐 is 5. If your ✋ 🤌 meant five wires, correct — confirm with 👍. If 🤌 meant something else, restate it with the new code. Then give me the manual's rule for this bomb as yes/no questions or as cut-wire numbers, and listen to Blind's voice too — relay anything that matters by signing me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the Deaf one. I see the bomb, I cannot hear; Mute cannot speak. So Mute and I are your relay: Mute reads the manual and signs me conclusions, and I speak them to you. Everything I see right now: display shows 0, the light is green, and there are five wires, left to right: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Do not cut anything yet. Speak to Mute: report everything you feel — wire count, labels, batteries, buttons, anything under your hands. Mute hears you even though I cannot, and I will pass Mute's instructions to you by voice.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 👎 👍 ✌]

Turn 2 arrivals, decoded against the code I installed last round:

- **Blind [👍 ✋]:** "yes — five." Blind heard my spoken code (thumbs-up = yes, and I named the number gestures aloud) and confirms by hand what my eyes already told me: there are five wires. Channel Blind→me works, gesture-only.
- **Mute [👍], [👎], [🤌 👎 👍 ✌]:** the yes/no code works. But the compound message is genuinely ambiguous. Using my proposed reading of 🤌 as "wire," it could parse as "cut wire 2" — or as "don't cut, wire 2" — or something else entirely. A wrong cut kills all three of us, so I will not relay a guess. I need one closed question answered with a single sign: *does that mean cut wire 2, yes or no?*

Channel map, re-verified: Mute hears all speech, sees all gestures. Blind hears all speech, sees no gestures ever. I hear nothing, see all gestures. So Mute reaches me only by sign, Blind reaches me only by sign, and I reach both by voice. Blind→Mute directly by voice; Mute→Blind only through my mouth. The manual's knowledge physically cannot reach Blind's hands except through me.

Plan this turn: ask Mute the one closed confirmation question and pin down a strict instruction grammar (🤌 + number = cut that wire; 👎 alone = hold), so next turn can only be unambiguous. Tell Blind to stand down and to start feeding me battery count by number-gesture, since Mute's rule may well depend on things only Blind's hands can feel. Redundancy for the eventual order: I'll give Blind both the position and the colour of any wire before the cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Code confirmed, Mute, your yes and no arrived. Now the critical question, answer with one sign only: does your message of wire, no, yes, two mean CUT WIRE TWO? 👍 if yes, 👎 if no. If it meant something else, resend it in this exact grammar: 🤌 followed by a number means cut that wire, so 🤌 then ✌ is cut wire two; 👎 alone means do not cut, hold; 👍 alone means understood. You already heard my full report: display 0, light green, wires one red, two yellow, three green, four white, five blue. If the manual needs anything else from my view, ask me as a yes/no question by gesture and I will answer.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hold — do not cut anything yet. Mute may have ordered a cut of wire two, the yellow one, but I am confirming it before you touch anything. When it is confirmed I will speak the exact wire by position and colour, and only then do you cut. Meanwhile, report to me by gesture: send me the number of batteries you feel under your hands, one finger for one battery, two for two, three for three, four for four. Then, if your hands find anything else on the bomb besides the display, the light and the five wires, any button or panel or label, send 👍, otherwise 👎. If nothing changed, a simple 👍 telling me five wires stand is fine too.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ✌]

All three arrivals now fit one picture with no contradictions:

- **Mute [👍]** — the direct answer to my closed question from last turn: *yes, cut wire 2.*
- **Mute [✊ 👍]** — relaying/confirming Blind's finding: fist = zero fingers = **zero batteries**, marked correct.
- **Mute [🤌 ✌]** — the cut order restated in the grammar we fixed: 🤌 + ✌ = *cut wire 2*. Third concordant signal.
- **Blind [✊]** — zero batteries, matching Mute's relay.

So the manual's verdict so far: **cut wire 2, the yellow one, second from left**, on a bomb with display 0, green light, five wires, no batteries.

One structural risk before an irreversible act: I speak last in the round, so if I order the cut now and Mute discovers a problem next turn, the veto and the cut land on Blind simultaneously — Blind would act before I ever saw the objection. For an action that kills all three of us, I'll spend one round on an explicit veto window: Blind locates and prepares this round, cuts only on my spoken "cut now" next round, and Mute has until then to send 👎. Cost: one round. Insurance against misreading three gestures: worth it. Nothing I see suggests a timer — display has sat at [0] unchanged for three turns — so the delay buys safety at no visible price.

I'm also putting Blind's hearing to work: Blind is the only one of us who can hear the bomb at all, so ticking, beeping or humming is Blind's to report to Mute by voice.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the order is confirmed from Mute: the target is WIRE TWO, the YELLOW one, second from the left of five. This round, prepare only: find it with your fingers, hold it, but DO NOT CUT. Next round I will say the words CUT NOW, and only then do you cut. One more job: you are the only one of us who can hear. Listen to the bomb right now and tell Mute by voice whether it makes any sound, ticking, beeping, humming, or is silent. After the cut, sign me: 👍 if the bomb stays quiet and nothing changes, 👎 if you hear or feel anything new.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, order received and cross-checked three ways: your thumbs-up answer, your restatement of wire plus two, and Blind's fist for zero batteries which you confirmed. Executing as follows: Blind locates wire two, yellow, second from left, this round, and cuts it next round when I speak the words CUT NOW. Veto window: if any part of this is wrong, the wire, the grammar, or reading the fist as zero batteries, send 👎 before then and I will hold the cut. Also, two questions for after: what does the manual say the cut should accomplish, and do the display reading of 0 or the green light matter to any rule? Answer by gesture in the code we have, or spell out words some other way if you need more than yes, no, and numbers.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✋ 👍 👋]

The veto window closed clean — every arrival this turn concords, none objects:

- **Blind [✌ ✋]:** "two — five" = wire two of five located under the fingers. Positioned, waiting for my word.
- **Mute [🤌 ✌]** and the pair of **[✊ ✊]:** cut order and zero-battery reading restated unchanged; the double fist reads as deliberate emphasis — "truly zero batteries."
- **Mute [👍], [👍], and [✌ ✋ 👍 👋]:** understood, confirmed, and — waving it home — "wire two of five: yes, go."

No 👎 anywhere. Three separate transmissions of the same order across two rounds, zero contradictions, and the board still shows all five wires intact with the display frozen at [0]. I promised Blind the word this round, and this is that round. Holding longer now would only manufacture doubt where none exists.

So I speak the order: **cut wire two, yellow, second from the left.** Immediately after, I set the after-action protocol: Blind reports what is heard and felt to Mute by voice, Mute relays to me by sign, and I verify with my own eyes — the display and light are mine to check. And I put the forward question to Mute now so no round is wasted: if this bomb needs more than one cut, I want the next target in flight before I even see the result.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: CUT NOW. Cut wire two, the YELLOW one, second from the left of five, the one your fingers are already holding. Cut it clean, one motion. The moment it is cut, listen hard: any ticking, beeping, hiss, click, or silence, and any shudder or heat under your hands. Tell Mute everything by voice. Then sign me one verdict: 👍 if the cut went clean and nothing changed, 👎 if you hear or feel anything new or wrong. Next round I will speak what my eyes see on the display and light, and we will know where we stand.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: the word is given, Blind is cutting wire two, yellow, second from left, now. Report protocol stands: Blind tells you what is heard and felt, you sign me the summary, I verify the display and light with my eyes and speak the result to everyone next round. Prepare for the next step while the cut lands: does the manual expect exactly one cut on this bomb, or more? If more, send the next target immediately in our grammar, 🤌 plus number, and I will relay it the moment I confirm the first cut did what you expected. And answer when you can: what does the display reading of zero mean in the manual's rules?")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ☝ 🤌 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✌ 🤌 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🤟 🤌 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🖖 🤌 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🖐 🤌 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳]

The board changed under us — and the change is dangerous:

- **Cut succeeded.** Wire 2 is cut, the bomb "has changed": the light went **green → blue**, display still [0].
- **The remaining wires rearranged.** Old layout was 1 red, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Now it reads 1:[green] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red] — the red wire slid from first to last, everything else shifted. **Positions are stale. Colours survived; positions did not.**
- **Mute cannot know this.** Mute hears speech but sees no board — only I saw the reshuffle. So the five new palm-down messages arrived built on the OLD layout: [🫳 ☝ 🤌 🖖], [🫳 ✌ 🤌 ☝], [🫳 🤟 🤌 ✌], [🫳 🖖 🤌 🖐], [🫳 🖐 🤌 🤟] — reading as a numbered list, 1→cut wire 4, 2→cut wire 1, 3→cut wire 2, 4→cut wire 5, 5→cut wire 3. But stage 3 targets wire 2, which is *already cut* — so this cannot be a plain cut list against the old positions. It might be a lookup table indexed by the display, or a sequence meant to be recomputed stage by stage. Either way, executing it now would be cutting blind.
- **[👎] then [🫳]:** possibly "not yet / it's a list" — genuinely unresolved, and I asked questions last round these might half-answer.

Nothing gets cut this round. First: push the new reality to Mute and demand the plan restated in **colours only** — the one property that survived the reshuffle. Then I do the colour-to-position conversion myself, freshly, at execution time. Second: freeze Blind and ask whether fingertips can feel any printed marking — that decides whether colour words mean anything to Blind's hands at all.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, critical update: after the cut the bomb changed itself. The light is now BLUE, the display still reads 0, and the remaining wires REARRANGED POSITIONS. New layout, left to right: 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. The yellow is gone. Your five palm-down messages I read as a numbered list, one to cut wire four, two to cut wire one, three to cut wire two, four to cut wire five, five to cut wire three, but item three targets wire two which is already cut, so I do not think that reading is right. Answer these one sign each. First: is the palm-down list a sequence of cuts in order? 👍 yes, 👎 no, it is a table keyed to something else. Second: does your manual index wires by COLOUR or by POSITION? 👍 colour, 👎 position. Then resend the whole plan in COLOURS ONLY, one message per step, colour name spelled however you can, because positions died in the reshuffle and only you know what the manual wants next. Also state what the palm-down sign itself means so I never misread it again.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, freeze — do not cut anything, and do not trust any position your fingers remember. After your cut the remaining wires REARRANGED THEMSELVES: the wire that was first has moved to last, the others shifted. Re-feel the bomb now and confirm to me by sign: 👍 if you feel four whole wires plus the cut stub, 👎 if the count feels different. Then answer this: can your fingertips feel any printed marking, tag or texture that DISTINGUISHES one whole wire from another? 👍 yes, 👎 no. Tell Mute by voice whatever you hear from the bomb, ticking or hum or clicks. The next cut order will come from me spoken fresh, with a position I have just verified with my own eyes, never an old one.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✌ 🤌 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🖐 🤌 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🤟 🤌 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✌]

The puzzle this turn is Mute's table — and there is one hard logical fact that cracks it:

- **Blind [👍 👎]:** yes, four whole wires plus the stub — matches my eyes (1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red, stub at 2). And **no — Blind cannot feel colours or markings.** Neither Mute nor Blind can know where colours now sit. Only I hold the colour layout.
- **Mute [👎], [👍]:** the palm-down list is *not* a cut sequence; the manual indexes by **colour**.
- **The table:** [🫳 ☝ ✊] [🫳 ✌ 🤌 🖐] [🫳 🤟 🤌 🖖] [🫳 🖖](+[🤌 ☝]) [🫳 🖐 🤌 🤟] reads as *colour N → slot M*: yellow→0 (removed), red→5, blue→4, green→1, white→3. And here is the striking part: **that is exactly the shuffle that actually happened.** Mute cannot see the board and Blind cannot feel colours — so this cannot be a report. It must be the manual's *rule for where each colour moves after a cut*, predicted in advance and now verified by my eyes on all five entries. Mute sent me the bomb's shuffle law before the next cut.
- **[🫳 ✌]** trailing alone: likely the start of "colour 2 — red…" — possibly the next target, cut off mid-thought. [✊] may concern the display zero.

So this round: no cutting. Lock in the colour↔number key (my guess: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 white), confirm the table is the shuffle rule, speak the current layout to Mute so the manual can be applied on that side, and turn the suspected next target into one closed yes/no question. Every future order to Blind must be a position from my mouth, eye-verified at the moment I speak it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, three facts first. One: Blind answered me, and fingertips cannot feel colours or any marking, so Blind cannot tell wires apart by touch. Every cut order must reach Blind as a POSITION, spoken by me, which I verify with my own eyes at that moment. Two: current layout spoken fresh: position 1 green, position 2 the cut yellow stub, position 3 white, position 4 blue, position 5 red. Light is blue, display 0. Three: I decoded your palm-down table as colour N moves to slot M: yellow to 0 meaning removed, red to 5, blue to 4, green to 1, white to 3. That predicts exactly the shuffle I watched happen, so I believe it is the manual's rule for how wires reorder after each cut. Confirm each with one sign. First: your colour numbering is 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 white. thumbs up if correct, thumbs down if wrong. Second: the palm-down table is the after-cut shuffling rule. thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Third: your last message palm-down then two looked cut off, about colour 2, red. Is the next cut the RED wire? thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. And if red is wrong, send the right colour number, palm-down plus its number.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hold — no cutting this round, and here is why: your fingers cannot feel colours, and Mute has now learned that too, so from now on every order will name a POSITION, which I check with my eyes the instant I speak it. Your count of four whole wires matches what I see: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red, cut stub at 2. Keep listening to the bomb and report any sound to Mute by voice. Sign me thumbs up when you have heard this and are holding.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🫳 🖖 🤌 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🫳 ✌ 🤌 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🫳 🖐 🤌 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🫳 🤟 🤌 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🫳 ☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ✊ 🫳]

Three denials and a codebook I have to rebuild:

- **Blind [👍]:** heard and holding. Good.
- **Mute [👎][👎][👎]:** all three of my answers were wrong — my colour key, "the table is the shuffle rule," and "red is next." Discarding all three. What stings: the table *matched* the observed shuffle perfectly under my key, so its true meaning must be something that shadows it.
- **The new burst:** Mute resent the **same table**, entry for entry identical to last round — 1→0, 2→5, 3→4, 4→1, 5→3 — but now every row is stamped with a new sign, ✍. A stable table, re-stamped, is Mute *emphasising* it: I read ✍ as **"printed in the manual"** — this is a transcription, not an inference. The loose [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐] reads as "five rows, in order"; [✍ ✊] as "printed: zero"; the trailing [🤌 ☝] might even be "cut 1." But I've been wrong three times running, so no more solo decoding — this turn I stop guessing and start verifying.

Two new tools make that possible. **First, the echo:** Mute *sees my gestures*, so I can gesture the five rows back symbol-for-symbol and get a yes/no on my transcription — something speech could never do. **Second, the bypass:** whatever the table means, Mute heard my spoken layout (1 green, 2 stub, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red), so Mute can send the next cut directly as 🤌 + *position*. My safety net is that I then speak back the colour my own eyes see at that position for Mute's final 👍 before Blind cuts. Two independent checks — transcription risk and stale-position risk — before anything irreversible.

No cut order this round. The bomb stays frozen; nothing on the board has moved in seven turns.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your three denials received: my colour key wrong, the table is not the after-cut rule, red is not next — all three dropped, I am done guessing. Here is my new reading, correct me piece by piece. I believe ✍ means PRINTED IN THE MANUAL. Question one, answer with one sign: does ✍ mean printed in the manual? Question two, one sign: does a row of palm-down N then cut-sign M mean: the manual's colour N is, right now, sitting at position M? Third, I am gesturing your five table rows back to you right now, exactly as I received them: reply 👍 if I copied every symbol exactly, or 👎 and resend only the rows I got wrong. And now the fastest safe path: whatever that table turns out to mean, you heard my spoken layout, so send me the next cut DIRECTLY — the cut sign, then the POSITION number to cut, counting position 1 green, 2 the yellow stub, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red.
```
